hints: Focus on gas volumes at the same temperature and pressure, since volume ratio is exactly the same as mole ratio for gases.
Notice that 10 cm3 of J gives 20 cm3 of CO2, so one molecule of J must produce two molecules of CO2 and therefore contains two carbon atoms.
Compare 10 cm3 of J giving 5 cm3 of N2, remembering each N2 has two N atoms, to work out how many N atoms are in one molecule of J.
walkthrough:
**Use Avogadro's principle for gases**

All volumes are measured at the same T and P, so gas volume is directly proportional to moles. We can treat volumes like moles.

$$\text{volume ratio} = \text{mole ratio}$$

**Find the number of carbon atoms in J**

10 cm3 of J produces 20 cm3 of $\text{CO}_2$. That is a 1 to 2 ratio.

$$10 \text{ J} \rightarrow 20 \text{ CO}_2$$
So 1 molecule of J gives 2 molecules of $\text{CO}_2$, which means 2 C atoms per J. All three formulas, 1, 2 and 3, contain $\text{C}_2$, so all pass the carbon test.

**Find the number of nitrogen atoms in J**

10 cm3 of J produces 5 cm3 of $\text{N}_2$. That is a 2 to 1 ratio.

$$2\text{J} \rightarrow 1\text{N}_2$$
One $\text{N}_2$ molecule contains 2 N atoms, so 2 molecules of J contain 2 N atoms. This means 1 molecule of J contains 1 N atom.

**Check the three candidates**

Statement 1 is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{N}_2$ with 2 N atoms, so 10 cm3 would give 10 cm3 of $\text{N}_2$, not 5 cm3. Statement 1 is false.

Statements 2 ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{N}$) and 3 ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_7\text{N}$) both have $\text{C}_2$ and $\text{N}_1$, exactly matching the data. So only 2 and 3 are possible.

options.A: This means 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statement 1 is wrong because C2H6N2 has two N atoms per molecule and would give twice as much N2 as observed. So A cannot be correct.
options.B: This means 1 and 2 only are correct. Statement 1 fails the nitrogen balance, 10 cm3 of C2H6N2 would produce 10 cm3 of N2, not 5 cm3. So B is incorrect.
options.C: This means 2 and 3 only are correct. Both C2H3N and C2H7N contain 2 carbons and 1 nitrogen, giving the observed 20 cm3 CO2 and 5 cm3 N2 from 10 cm3 of J. Well done if you spotted the 2 to 1 volume link for nitrogen.
options.D: This means 1 only is correct. Statement 1 is actually the one that is false, since its N2 volume would be double the experimental value. D is a trap if you forget that N2 contains two N atoms.
